event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: The fixed names used by these tests do not collide with other test runs or real containers. Details: failure_tests.rs uses fixed reserved names in absent-session, proxy-recovery, restart-failure and partial-admission tests (around lines 1089, 1221, 1398, 1460). Considered whether this violates the shared-machine naming contract or risks removing another run's resources. Fixture::new in provisioning/session_launch_failure_tests.rs:41-89 creates a separate Harness/store and constructs a new Commands instance per fixture; failure_tests.rs:135-146 gives that Commands its own State mutex, and PlaceCommands::run_bounded/run_with_input at lines 333-354 exclusively invoke the in-memory execute method. Container creation/removal at lines 531-547 and 684-687 mutate only this per-instance model. No real Podman process receives these names. Suggested bucket: other if it were a defect. Confidence: confirmed by source; no execution. proposed_drop: false positive, because each name is scoped to a separate in-memory command fake rather than shared Podman storage. possible_cover: none; coverage sources were not searched. Could-be-highest: false; no route to real resources or user work is present. Caveat: this conclusion covers the assigned fake's names, not unrelated runtime harnesses.

event.summary: Fixture failure cannot orphan a real container through these injected seams
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: An assertion or setup failure in the assigned tests does not leave a real container or independently running supervisor behind. Details: Considered the lifetime risk from Fixture::prepare's ten-second timeout (session_launch_failure_tests.rs:152-174): it drops the preparation waiter, while podman.rs:985-1036 and tensorlake/build.rs:679-725 deliberately keep preparation in a spawned task. That timeout therefore is not evidence that the background operation has stopped. Source refutation of an escaped real-resource consequence: Fixture::new at lines 41-89 injects Commands and E2eProvisioningBackend before provider use; failure_tests.rs:318-355 and 357-749 implement command calls and mutations entirely in memory, and rest_harness.rs:372-438 implements transport with Tokio duplex streams and spawned scripted peers. Fixture and Harness own their temporary directories (session_launch_failure_tests.rs:18-27; rest_harness.rs:710-726). ConnectionManager Drop shuts down its actors (manager.rs:3137-3147); the farhelm_testtrace asynchronous wrapper owns and drops the per-test runtime even after a caught body unwind (farhelm-testtrace/src/lib.rs:994-1024), bounding detached async work to that test runtime. Suggested bucket: other if a tooling cleanup defect were established. Confidence: confirmed by source; no execution. proposed_drop: no established orphaned external resource, because the examined tasks have modeled command/backend/transport boundaries and a per-test runtime owner. possible_cover: none; excluded coverage sources were not read. Could-be-highest: false; no shipped user-work or security route is established. Caveats: this does not prove synchronous fixture draining before its temp directories drop, and it does not establish real Podman cleanup or behavior after real process termination. A timeout may leave the owned preparation task alive until test-runtime teardown; the claimed refutation is only of externally escaping container/supervisor state.

event.summary: Failure matrices distinguish requested boundaries from earlier setup errors
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: These failure tests do not pass solely because setup failed at an unrelated earlier stage. Details: Considered whether prearming failures before preparation and asserting generic errors could conceal missing fixture prerequisites or skipped intended phases. The command matrix asserts both result.is_err and Commands::failed()==phase (failure_tests.rs:821-861); hit records failed only when the selected phase is actually reached and consumes that fault (lines 219-233). The backend matrix additionally asserts the exact canonical helper/event and absence of prepared publication (869-887); Fixture::fail_backend selects podman:<64-hex-id> and backend_reached compares both target and event (session_launch_failure_tests.rs:194-233). E2eProvisioningBackend::action records the event, then returns the selected failure (e2e.rs:208-236); production build.rs:95-114 and 294-369 propagate the backend/installer failures. The successful cold premise enumerates both phase sets before checking reuse (failure_tests.rs:779-814). The cleanup-refusal test lacks a separate failed()==packages assertion, but its fake refuses removal only after State.failed is set by the selected command fault; observing retained canonical helper plus cleanup failure therefore establishes that prerequisite through the fake's own fault gate (failure_tests.rs:657-669, 895-911). Lost/invalid commit tests assert the selected commit was visited (918-936), and their unique lost_commit configuration can return the intended injected error only after inserting the owned image and tag. Absent helper/session tests explicitly check failed()==selected and the absent-resource premise before retry/deletion assertions (1106-1136, 1156-1193). Suggested bucket: other if misleading test evidence were established. Confidence: confirmed by source; no execution. proposed_drop: the suspected unrelated-error false pass is refuted by phase/target assertions and the source fault gates for the assigned cases. possible_cover: none; excluded coverage sources were not read. Could-be-highest: false; no shipped security or loss-of-work route is established. Caveats: the evidence validates orchestration over modeled command/backend results, not real Podman, systemd, proxy-file bytes or remote filesystem effects. The production cleanup path runs reconcile_helpers then retire_images before publishing failure (build.rs:267-290); the model checks canonical removal, stopped-before-commit, durable tags-before-commit, and nonforced unused-image removal, while intentionally keeping absent uncertain sends pending. It does not simulate delayed external materialization; the assertions instead verify that uncertainty prevents immediate forgetting or retry.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: the proxy privacy test may give false assurance that metacharacter/newline values are inherited exactly, because its expected prefix comes from the production serializer itself. Source basis: failure_tests.rs:14-16 says the secret proves exact inheritance rather than lossy sanitization; cold_build_sends_exact_proxy_values_only_as_private_input obtains expected exports from build::proxy_exports(&values), then compares private input with that prefix. The command model does not execute input, and the contextual backend install-byte method ignores content. Suspected consequence is an overstated exact-inheritance test oracle, separate from the correctly tested absence of a marker in argv and from g065/l1's confirmed production empty-variable persistence issue. Checks so far: full assigned patch and earlier backend implementation reads establish the shared helper and modeled I/O, but need targeted recheck of precise assertion scope, serializer transformation and in-range persistence before conclusion. Exact missing premise: whether another assertion in this test independently distinguishes lossy serialization of the metacharacter/newline value, or whether the claim is intentionally confined to transport serialization after that helper. Next source checks: read the full test, proxy_exports, and pinned-range history of the assigned file. event.summary: Proxy test's shared serializer cannot prove its exact-inheritance claim
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b.

## TLDR
The new proxy privacy test claims to detect lossy handling of metacharacters and newlines, but computes its expected bytes with the same serializer as production. A regression that changes those values inside that serializer can pass, giving false assurance about exact inheritance. This is a test-oracle/documentation defect, not an observed production proxy or credential failure.

## Details
The fixture value's comment explicitly promises that including shell metacharacters and a newline means a passing privacy test 'proves that exact inheritance was not replaced with lossy sanitization' (failure_tests.rs:12-14). The test cold_build_sends_exact_proxy_values_only_as_private_input creates the original value map at :987-990 but derives its expected prefix by calling build::proxy_exports(&values) at :991. Its exact-value assertion at :1027-1029 only checks input.starts_with(that prefix). Production Podman::script calls this same build::proxy_exports on the actual place values (environment/podman.rs:356). event.summary: Synthesized ownership labels limit the fake without contradicting its asserted failure contracts
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: this command fake is not independent evidence that real containers receive or retain ownership labels, but its current failure-cleanup assertions do not claim to test label tampering. Details: During the separate discovery pass, considered whether container/image inspect fabricates ownership evidence and thereby invalidates this file's cleanup tests. Source confirms that container inspect emits this Commands instance's helm and dev recipe labels (:388-391); run parses role but does not retain helm/recipe argv labels (:422-432, :520-534); image inspect similarly synthesizes labels for modeled owned images (:396-405). Thus a missing actual helm label in run argv would not itself be detected here. The file introduces a model of provider command/backend boundaries (:1-3), and its particular ownership assertion explicitly covers model-owned images retaining durable provider records (:259-292). Its failure matrices verify phase reach, durable helper/image records and canonical cleanup, not rejection of a relabeled or foreign resource; no such foreign/relabeled fixture is introduced in the assigned tests. The canonical-identity comment at :78-79 concerns distinct model IDs, rather than promising exhaustive independent label verification. There is therefore no separate demonstrated false oracle for those stated assertions, and requiring this model to test every ownership boundary would be a new coverage request. This differs from l1, whose exact-inheritance sensitivity is expressly promised and source-refuted. Suggested bucket: other if a specific test-oracle defect were established. Confidence: confirmed source limitation, no execution. proposed_drop: no established contradiction with the assigned tests' actual assertions or an explicit label-verification claim; retain as a bounded model limitation rather than a finding. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Could-be-highest: false for this test-model limitation; no shipped security or destructive behavior is established or dropped. Caveat: the fake cannot be cited as real-container label/lifecycle evidence, and an explicitly label-focused test using this unmodified oracle would require independent label state or assertions.
